blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ Refuses to Build the Masjid Like the Buildings in Shaam

Hadhrat Khaalid bin Ma'daan narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) were once measuring the Masjid with a stick. Coming out of his room, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What are you two doing?" They replied, "We wish to construct the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ like the buildings of Shaam are built. The expenses shall be borne by the Ansaar." "Bring me that stick," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed. He then took the stick from them and walked away with it. When he reached his door, Rasulullaah ﷺ threw the stick away and said, "Never! (The Masjid should never be built like that!) It should be made of grass, sticks and roof like the shelter of Moosa (AS). Death is much nearer at hand." When someone asked what the shelter of Hadhrat Moosa (AS) was like, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "When he stood up, his head touched the roof." [^1]
The Masjid is Extended during the Periods of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)

Hadhrat Naafi narrates, "Hadhrat Umar (RA) extended the Masjid from the pillars to the Maqsoorah (the room built for the Imaam). He said, 'Had I not heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'We ought to extend our Masjid', I would never have extended it." [^2]

Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) that during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Masjid was built with unbaked bricks, the roof was made of palm branches and the pillars were palm trunks. While Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) made no extensions to the Masjid, Hadhrat Umar (RA) did. He however built the Masjid as it was during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, using unbaked bricks, palm branches and replacing the pillars of palm trunks. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) changed the building and made a large extension. He used decorative stones and plaster for the walls with decorative stones for the pillars and teakwood for the roof. [^3]

Hadhrat Atiyya narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "During the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the pillars of the Masjid consisted of palm trunks with the top shaded with palm branches. When this deteriorated during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he rebuilt it also using palm trunks and branches. When it again deteriorated during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), he had it rebuilt with baked bricks and it has remained standing to this day." [^4]
